points.quote: `workbench.desktop.main.ts` imports `workbench.common.main.js` first. It then adds desktop-only code from `electron-browser/` folders.
`workbench.web.main.ts` also imports `workbench.common.main.js` first. It then adds `browser/web.main.js` and web-specific implementations
`src/vs/workbench/workbench.common.main.ts` is the shared entry point. ... `workbench.desktop.main.ts` imports `workbench.common.main.js` first.
The same service interface usually gets a different implementation in each build. The web build registers a `*.web` or `browser` one.
a feature's code is only bundled and loaded if one of the entry files imports it, directly or transitively.
It is a long list of side-effect imports (`import './contrib/...contribution.js'`). ... To make a feature appear in both, add it to the common file.
